veranderings.voor: 'n groot muur hou dit in 'n dam
veranderings.na: 'n groot muur keer dit in 'n dam op
veranderings.rede: Water is 'opgekeer' by a dam wall; 'hou dit in 'n dam' is vague and less idiomatic.

veranderings.voor: Die dam sak dan laer en laer.
veranderings.na: Die water in die dam sak dan laer en laer.
veranderings.rede: It is the water level that drops, not the dam itself; clearer for a Grade 5 reader.

veranderings.voor: lang pad en nie sy begin nie
veranderings.na: lang pad, nie die begin nie
veranderings.rede: The contrast reads more naturally as 'X, nie Y nie' and 'sy begin' is a stiff pronoun reference.

veranderings.blok: Nie elke kraan is naby nie
veranderings.rede: Afrikaans idiom is 'op ander plekke', not 'in ander plekke'.

veranderings.blok: Wat jy self kan doen om water te spaar
veranderings.rede: Natural Afrikaans uses the possessive here, and it parallels 'jou hande inseep' in the same item.

veranderings.blok: Hoe ons die water skoon hou
veranderings.voor: Was met seep in 'n bak en nie in die rivier self nie.
veranderings.na: Was met seep in 'n bak, nie in die rivier self nie.
veranderings.rede: The contrast 'X, nie Y nie' is smoother and matches the first item of the same list.

vlae.teks: Wanneer water in die lug optrek en 'n nat plek daardeur droër word.
vlae.rede: A definition that opens with 'Wanneer' does not define the verb itself; rewording it to start with the verb ('Om ...') would change how the definition is built, so it is left for the reviewer or writer.

vlae.blok: Hoekom jou liggaam elke dag water nodig het
vlae.teks: Kos word ook met water gekook en klere daarmee gewas. Die toilet spoel met water, en mielies in die land groei daarmee.
vlae.rede: The heading speaks of the body's need for water, but half the block is about other uses of water (cooking, washing, toilets, crops, a clinic); a heading fix would touch content, so it is only flagged.
